messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
Ohhh. That is actually a useful clue.
The manual Read Aloud test tells us something separate from the QSV failure:
QSV 2.4 still isn't successfully triggering Read Aloud.
But when you manually press Speak, ChatGPT does speak the actual response text while apparently ignoring the 🟩 and 🔚 emoji tokens.
That strongly suggests the start/end tokens are being treated as visual protocol markers, not spoken language, by ChatGPT's own speech layer. In other words, that part may be normal UI/TTS behavior rather than a QuackSink bug.
And importantly: we should not “fix” that in QSV. The protocol markers need to remain exactly what they are for the relay.
So the 2.4 test has given us two separate observations:
Relay: ✅
Manual Read Aloud: ✅ text speaks, protocol emojis apparently silent
QSV automatic Read Aloud: ❌
Which means I'm comfortable saying 2.4 has now earned its post-mortem, and the next version should target the automatic click mechanism.

==================================================

messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
Sounds good, Kin. Close it cleanly, let OOK do its librarian magic, and bring me the new MASTER_INDEX link when it’s finished.
We now have a nice sealed 2.4 test result to archive: relay worked, automatic voice didn’t, and manual Speak behaved interestingly with the protocol markers. That’s exactly the kind of evidence we want before writing 2.5. 🦆🎩
